{"notes":"TRIED 2026-11-24 AND BACKED OUT. The bead called this small. It is not, and
the reason is worth recording so the next attempt does not repeat it.

THE OBVIOUS FIX, which does work as far as it goes: crate-jmap's
`Dispatcher<CallerCtx>` carries one value of the caller's choosing to every
handler, and the agent passes the account `Id`. Nothing in mimid reads
`cx.caller` at all (grep: zero uses), so widening it to a
`Caller { account: Id, login: Option<Login> }` looked like a handful of
signatures plus the two dispatch sites.

WHY IT IS NOT SMALL. `AgentChat` implements crate-jmap's `JmapAccounts`,
`ChatStore` and `DelegateJmapReads` with `type CallerCtx = Id`, and
`register_chat_handlers` takes `Dispatcher<B::CallerCtx>`. So changing the
dispatcher's context forces `AgentChat::CallerCtx` to change, and with it
`caller: &Id` in every `ChatStore` and `JmapAccounts` method in
crates/mimid-agent-jmap/src/backend.rs. Worse, those methods delegate to an
inner `MemoryBackend`, whose `CallerCtx` IS `Id` and cannot change (it is
crate-jmap's), so every delegation would have to translate `Caller` back to
`&Id`. That is dozens of signatures in the heart of the chat backend, for a
`created_by` string.

WHAT IT IS WORTH. The field reads `jmap` instead of `jmap (phone)`. The
front end is already recorded, the CLI records `cli`, and IRC records
`irc (<credential>)`, so the only thing missing is WHICH DEVICE asked over
JMAP, in a listing that already shows last-used time and peer.

WHAT WOULD NOT WORK, so nobody tries it: a task-local (the dispatcher spawns
each call on its own task, which does not inherit one); passing the login
through `args` (they are the client's); or putting something other than the
account id in the caller context (crate-jmap's MemoryBackend uses it for its
own permission checks).

DO IT WHEN something else makes `AgentChat::CallerCtx` change anyway — the
Matrix front end (bead mimid-e13m.7) wants per-device tokens and may well
need the credential in a handler, and that is the moment to widen it once for
both."}
